caseno: Appeal from Appellate Decree No.886 of 1961.
lawyer:
Mohitur Rahman Chowdhury ------ For the Appellant. 
Md. Fazlul Karim ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Juran Sheikh being dead, his legal heirs—Md. Nurul Hussain being dead his legal heirs—Kadbanu Bewa & other  ------ Appellants.
Vs.
Mamirunnessa Khatun being dead her legal heirs Mobarak Sarkar & others  ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 3. The suit was resisted by defendants 1,7 and 8 by filing a joint written statement but the defendant No.1 Juran Sheikh alone contested the suit at the trial. In the written statement it was contended, inter alia, that Bonde Ali Sheikh predecessor-in-interest of defendant Nos.1 and 7 to 16 had been in possession of the suit land with their homestead thereon for about 40 years as a tenant under the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiff; and the under raiyati interest recorded in C.S. 841 was at first held by Mebarulla Sheikh at a jama of Rs. 22/- under Rabim Baksh and others. Meharulla Sheikh sold his interest to Baharullah Bepari and the latter held the under raiyati at a jama of Rs.26-4 annas; and the Baharullah Bepari died leaving four sons Ashatulla and three others, five daughters, two widows and one of the daughters Subjan died leaving Chotomai as her heir:— and that Chotomai bibi also died leaving her heir Dholi Mai but she was not made a party. Therefore, the decree obtained in the rent suit was not rent decree and consequently the alleged rent sale did not affect the defendants. It was further contended by the defendants that under the under raiyati recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 841 standing in the name of Ashatultah Sarkar and others there are several sub-leases or under raiyati interests of second and third degree recorded in C.S. Khatian Nos. 844, 847 and 843. The under raiyati in respect of 1.84 acres recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 848 was held by Bonde Ali Sheikh and Juran Sheikh under Meharullah at a jama of Rs. 15/- under a registered patta dated the 13th November, 1919, corresponding to 27th Kartic 1326 B.S. Jama was enhanced to Rs.15.5 annas after Bahrulla purchased the under raiyati interest from Meharulla when Juran Sheikh and Bonde Ali Sheikh executed a registered kabuliyat dated 26th November, 1927 corresponding 10th Agrabayan, 1334 B.S. for cultivation and residential purpose. Thus the under raiyati interest held by the defendants under Baharulla has neither been affected by the alleged rent sale nor the plaintiff on the basis of that rent sale is entitled to get khas possession of the land by evicting the defendants. The under raiyati in respect of 40 acre recorded in C.S. Khatian No.847 was held only by Bonde Ali Sheikh at a jama of Rs. 4-8 annas under Khalil Mahmud Mondal whose interest has been recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 844 and so long the interest of Khalil Mahmud is not made khas, the subordinate interest of the defendants also cannot be made khas and that in any view of the matter the interest of the defendants being protected under the law, the plaintiff cannot get khas possession by evicting the defendants, contended that the plaintiff cannot have a decree for khas possession, inasmuch as, with the consent of the landlords, namely, Rahim Baksha and others the under raiyaties were created, and as such the transfer being valid in law, and also the defendants and their predecessor-in-interest having their homestead in the suit land appertaining to the said under raiyati interest, the plaintiff cannot get khas possession by evicting the defendants, because the interest of the defendants in suit land is protected.
